rule: Contact order: spark and hit sound on the contact frame; then a shared freeze set on both sides (attacker pausetime[0], target pausetime[1]), with the target freeze assigned only when not already in hit-stun; then a flash in the air states (3 frames) and rumble by tier; then the knock slide, whose x velocity is multiplied by 0.6 once time reaches slideTime; then screen shake on fall or bounce from one shared EnvShake object that a new trigger overwrites rather than sums. Freeze length is simulation state in the engine (c.hitPauseTime counts down in the update loop), so it belongs in the server event.
keep: Order: contact spark and sound, then shared freeze, then flash, then slide that eases, then shake on fall or bounce
Target freeze assigned only when not already in hit-stun (no stacking by addition)
One shared shake object per screen (new trigger overwrites)
3-frame white flash on airborne hit; 20-frame red flash on guard break
Commands pressed during the freeze are buffered, not lost (deprecated global toggle; keep per command)
change: Freeze length comes from the server event, both clients identical
Our own colours, sounds and shake shape
Rumble only on the heavy tier, none on light hits
Shake takes the max across stacked hits, not an overwrite by the latest
look_test: Flag on the existing dummy duel, published to /preview/ with no release rows. Three switchable modes on one screen: A no feedback (baseline); B the ordered stack (spark and sound at contact, both frozen 4 and 6 frames, white flash, slide that eases, shake and rumble on heavy only); C B with three attackers piling onto one target to test the stacking rule. Dom judges: can he tell which hit landed in a three-on-one pile, and does heavy feel heavier than light with no number on screen.
